axes.name: Spatial composition and layout system
axes.purpose: Formalize regions, containment, grids, alignment, rhythm, density, hierarchy, and depth as reusable spatial relationships.

facets.name: Regions and containment
facets.question: Which regions, containers, boundaries, and nesting levels organize the interface?
inspect: page, shell, section, panel, card, inset, and overlay boundaries
container ownership, edge behavior, and nesting depth
full-bleed, bounded, sticky, fixed, and scrollable regions
screenshotLimits: a crop does not establish the full page boundary
a static frame does not prove sticky, fixed, or scroll ownership

facets.name: Grid, columns, and containers
facets.question: Which repeated tracks, gutters, margins, spans, and container relationships explain the visible geometry?
inspect: column count, span relationships, gutters, and outer margins
nested grids, repeated tracks, and alignment anchors
content width, readable width, and local overflow regions
screenshotLimits: exact grid measurements cannot be recovered from scaled pixels alone
one viewport does not establish breakpoint-specific tracks

facets.name: Spacing and vertical rhythm
facets.question: Which gap families and repetition ratios distinguish related, grouped, and separate content?
inspect: intra-control, intra-component, inter-component, section, and page gaps
repeated spacing families and exceptional gaps
baseline rhythm, row rhythm, and whitespace distribution
screenshotLimits: visual estimates do not prove exact token values
empty content can imitate intentional whitespace

facets.name: Alignment and proportion
facets.question: Which geometric and optical alignments create order and balance?
inspect: edge, center, baseline, decimal, icon, and optical alignment
dominant-to-supporting region proportions
aspect ratios and repeated geometry
screenshotLimits: optical alignment is an interpretation unless repeated evidence supports it
cropping can distort apparent proportion

facets.name: Density, depth, and salience
facets.question: How do whitespace, scale, contrast, depth, and repetition establish perceptual priority?
inspect: information density and control density by region
salience tiers, focal anchors, and quiet zones
surface layering, overlap, elevation, and depth cues
screenshotLimits: prominence does not prove product priority or usage frequency
a screenshot cannot prove dynamic elevation or scroll behavior

axes.name: Typography and content hierarchy
axes.purpose: Extract role-based type relationships, readability constraints, numeric treatment, and content behavior without guessing font identity.

facets.name: Type roles and scale
facets.question: Which semantic text roles exist and how are their sizes and weights related?
inspect: display, page title, section title, component title, body, label, metadata, caption, code, and data roles
relative size, weight, contrast, and spacing hierarchy
role reuse and intentional exceptions
screenshotLimits: font family and exact metrics cannot be identified from resemblance
a single sample does not establish a complete modular scale

facets.name: Metrics and readability
facets.question: Which relationships among size, line height, measure, tracking, and paragraph spacing preserve readability?
inspect: line-height-to-size relationships and text block measure
tracking, word spacing, paragraph rhythm, and dense-label treatment
readability floors and proposed calibration bounds
screenshotLimits: computed metrics require implementation evidence
visual sharpness is affected by capture scale and compression

facets.name: Emphasis and semantic hierarchy
facets.question: How do weight, color, case, decoration, and placement distinguish importance and meaning?
inspect: strong, subtle, interactive, warning, success, disabled, and placeholder text
capitalization, sentence case, title case, underlining, and emphasis patterns
heading continuity and label-value relationships
screenshotLimits: visual hierarchy does not establish semantic heading levels
color alone cannot establish text meaning

facets.name: Numerals and data typography
facets.question: How are values, units, signs, decimals, percentages, currencies, dates, and comparisons formatted and aligned?
inspect: tabular versus proportional alignment cues
unit placement, precision, signs, abbreviations, and large-number formatting
value, context, comparison, and timeframe hierarchy
screenshotLimits: glyph feature support cannot be proven from pixels
one locale does not establish alternate number or date formats

facets.name: Text overflow and language resilience
facets.question: How should text survive wrapping, clamping, long words, expansion, alternate scripts, and bidirectionality?
inspect: visible wrap, clamp, ellipsis, and growth zones
label and value collision risks
script, locale, RTL, and enlarged-text implications
screenshotLimits: short text does not prove an overflow policy
unseen scripts and directions remain proposed or unknown

axes.name: Color, surfaces, assets, and visual identity
axes.purpose: Extract semantic color relationships, surface hierarchy, shape language, iconography, imagery, and brand expression.

facets.name: Semantic color roles
facets.question: Which colors communicate background, content, action, status, selection, data, and focus roles?
inspect: canvas, surface, text, icon, border, action, status, selection, and focus roles
role pairings and contrast relationships
shared roles versus component-specific exceptions
screenshotLimits: capture pixels do not prove source color values
color appearance can be altered by compression and display profiles

facets.name: Surfaces and depth
facets.question: How do fills, borders, radii, elevation, overlays, and transparency express containment and depth?
inspect: surface tiers and nested surface relationships
border weight, radius families, shadow softness, and overlay treatment
flat, raised, inset, selected, disabled, and scrim relationships
screenshotLimits: exact blur, opacity, radius, and shadow values are not visually provable
dynamic elevation cannot be observed in a static frame

facets.name: Theme and contrast modes
facets.question: Which theme modes are evidenced and which semantic roles must remain stable across proposed modes?
inspect: light, dark, high-contrast, and branded theme evidence
surface inversion and semantic role persistence
contrast-sensitive pairings and non-color coding
screenshotLimits: one theme does not establish another theme
WCAG contrast requires measured implementation values

facets.name: Iconography, imagery, and illustration
facets.question: Which stroke, fill, geometry, crop, treatment, and semantic-role patterns form the asset grammar?
inspect: icon family, optical size, stroke, corner, cap, bounding box, and alignment
photo, avatar, illustration, logo, thumbnail, and decorative asset treatment
crop, ratio, mask, fallback, and placeholder implications
screenshotLimits: the exact icon or asset library cannot be identified reliably
licenses, alt text, source resolution, and fallbacks are not visible

facets.name: Visual identity and brand expression
facets.question: Which repeated visual choices establish tone, personality, distinctiveness, and emotional temperature?
inspect: shape language, saturation, contrast, illustration, photography, and decorative motifs
formal, editorial, technical, playful, premium, restrained, or expressive cues
brand moments versus neutral utility surfaces
screenshotLimits: visual tone does not establish brand strategy or intended audience
a small sample cannot prove the complete identity system

axes.name: Component morphology and composition
axes.purpose: Turn repeated controls and content structures into explicit anatomy, variant, state, density, composition, and exception contracts.

facets.name: Anatomy and slots
facets.question: Which required and optional parts make each repeated component recognizable and functional?
inspect: container, label, icon, value, supporting content, action, status, and media slots
required, optional, repeatable, and conditional parts
content ownership and slot order
screenshotLimits: repeated appearance does not prove a shared implementation component
hidden optional slots remain unknown

facets.name: Variants, sizing, and density
facets.question: Which size, density, emphasis, intent, and layout variants are visibly coherent?
inspect: compact, default, comfortable, prominent, subtle, and destructive relationships
height, padding, icon, label, and target-size relationships
variant selection conditions and unsupported combinations
screenshotLimits: one visible instance does not establish a variant family
target size and DOM box require implementation evidence

facets.name: State appearance
facets.question: How does anatomy remain stable across visible or required control and business states?
inspect: default, hover, focus, pressed, selected, disabled, read-only, loading, error, and success appearance
state-specific icon, text, border, surface, and geometry changes
non-color state indicators and preserved action access
screenshotLimits: unshown states are not observed
a state-looking appearance does not prove programmatic state

facets.name: Composition and reuse
facets.question: How may components combine, nest, align, repeat, or remain separate without collapsing hierarchy?
inspect: parent-child, sibling, group, toolbar, field, card, list, and section composition
spacing ownership and nested-surface limits
repetition, grouping, and responsive transformation
screenshotLimits: visual similarity alone does not establish shared component ownership
unseen combinations remain proposed or unknown

facets.name: Exceptions and anti-patterns
facets.question: Which deviations are intentional, and which combinations would break meaning, legibility, or consistency?
inspect: one-off emphasis, context-specific variants, and deliberate asymmetry
invalid nesting, density, duplication, and competing action patterns
conditions requiring a new component rather than another variant
screenshotLimits: rarity does not prove an intentional exception
an absent combination is not automatically forbidden

axes.name: Navigation, information architecture, and task flow
axes.purpose: Describe visible orientation, hierarchy, action priority, disclosure, and continuity without inventing unseen product worlds.

facets.name: Global and local navigation
facets.question: Which visible structures move between product areas, peer views, and local contexts?
inspect: rails, sidebars, bars, tabs, breadcrumbs, menus, steps, and contextual links
global versus local scope and nesting
persistent versus contextual navigation cues
screenshotLimits: one screen does not prove destinations or persistence
visual navigation does not prove route behavior

facets.name: Orientation and current location
facets.question: How does the interface show where the user is, what scope is active, and what changed?
inspect: selected navigation, headings, breadcrumbs, context labels, and active filters
parent, peer, child, and return-path cues
scope, account, workspace, object, and time-context anchors
screenshotLimits: active styling does not prove URL or programmatic selection
cropped context can hide orientation cues

facets.name: Information hierarchy and reading order
facets.question: In what order does the visible screen ask users to perceive, understand, decide, and act?
inspect: visual and probable semantic reading order
overview-to-detail, summary-to-evidence, and problem-to-action sequences
grouping, chunking, and cognitive load
screenshotLimits: visual order does not establish DOM order
a screenshot cannot prove comprehension or task success

facets.name: Action priority and decision points
facets.question: Which actions are primary, secondary, tertiary, contextual, destructive, or terminal?
inspect: placement, emphasis, grouping, repetition, and consequence cues
next-step, alternate, cancel, back, save, submit, and destructive actions
competing actions and dead-end risks
screenshotLimits: prominence does not prove frequency or business priority
real consequences and permissions remain unknown

facets.name: Disclosure and context continuity
facets.question: How does the interface reveal depth while preserving location, selection, scroll, and task context?
inspect: expanders, drawers, dialogs, inline details, master-detail, and drill-down cues
trigger-to-result spatial relationship
back, close, cancel, focus return, and context preservation requirements
screenshotLimits: closed content and transitions are not visible
focus, scroll, and history restoration require executed evidence

axes.name: Forms, input, and workflow integrity
axes.purpose: Extract data-entry, selection, validation, formatting, save, and recovery patterns for simple and complex workflows.

facets.name: Labels, instructions, and help
facets.question: How are fields named, explained, marked, grouped, and connected to supporting guidance?
inspect: visible labels, legends, descriptions, examples, units, placeholders, and required markers
instruction placement and progressive help
field groups, sections, and dependency explanations
screenshotLimits: visual proximity does not prove accessible association
placeholder text does not prove a persistent label

facets.name: Controls and selection models
facets.question: Which input, selection, search, filter, upload, date, and compound-control patterns are visible?
inspect: text, number, select, checkbox, radio, switch, date, file, segmented, combobox, and custom controls
single, multiple, range, hierarchical, and batch selection
clear, reset, reveal, browse, and direct-manipulation affordances
screenshotLimits: appearance does not prove native versus custom implementation
keyboard and touch behavior are not visible

facets.name: Validation and error recovery
facets.question: When, where, and how should constraints, errors, warnings, and correction paths appear?
inspect: inline, summary, blocking, advisory, and asynchronous validation cues
error specificity, preservation of input, and correction focus
success, partial success, conflict, and retry states
screenshotLimits: validation timing and server behavior are not observable in a static frame
absence of errors does not prove their design

facets.name: Workflow, save, and reversibility
facets.question: How are progress, dependencies, review, submission, autosave, cancellation, and undo represented?
inspect: single-step, staged, wizard, inline edit, bulk edit, review, and confirmation patterns
dirty, saving, saved, failed, draft, and conflict implications
cancel, back, undo, discard, and work-preservation requirements
screenshotLimits: autosave and persistence cannot be inferred from appearance
server-side effects and rollback remain unknown

facets.name: Formatting and sensitive data
facets.question: How should values survive masks, locale formats, precision, privacy, and mobile keyboard constraints?
inspect: dates, times, currencies, percentages, phone numbers, identifiers, and units
masked, revealed, copied, generated, and sensitive values
input mode, autofill, paste, scanning, and virtual-keyboard implications
screenshotLimits: actual input mode, autofill, paste, and masking behavior require implementation evidence
one locale does not establish parsing rules

axes.name: Data display, statistics, and visualization
axes.purpose: Extract the grammar of metrics, comparisons, tables, lists, charts, legends, precision, uncertainty, and scale.

facets.name: Statistics and KPI anatomy
facets.question: How are labels, primary values, units, context, comparison, trend, timeframe, target, and freshness displayed?
inspect: metric label, value, unit, qualifier, trend, delta, baseline, timeframe, target, status, and action
primary versus supporting metrics and repeated KPI grids
positive, negative, neutral, unavailable, partial, and stale presentations
screenshotLimits: color and arrows do not prove whether a change is beneficial
metric formulas, freshness, and business meaning remain unknown unless supplied

facets.name: Comparison and decision context
facets.question: What baseline, target, period, segment, denominator, ranking, or uncertainty is required to interpret a value?
inspect: absolute versus relative values and period-over-period comparison
benchmark, target, range, ranking, contribution, and segmentation
precision, rounding, units, signs, and explanatory context
screenshotLimits: a visible delta does not establish its calculation
missing context cannot be invented from layout

facets.name: Tables, lists, and dense collections
facets.question: How do rows, columns, metadata, hierarchy, actions, selection, and navigation preserve scanability at scale?
inspect: column roles, row anatomy, alignment, density, sticky cues, and action placement
sorting, filtering, grouping, pagination, expansion, selection, and batch-action cues
empty, partial, loading, error, long-content, and extreme-value behavior
screenshotLimits: visible controls do not prove sorting, filtering, pagination, or virtualization
one dataset does not establish scale behavior

facets.name: Charts and visual encodings
facets.question: Which question, marks, channels, axes, scales, legends, annotations, and interactions define each visualization?
inspect: bar, line, area, point, distribution, part-to-whole, flow, hierarchy, and spatial encodings
position, length, area, angle, color, shape, size, texture, and ordering channels
axes, scales, domains, baselines, legends, labels, gridlines, annotations, and reference lines
screenshotLimits: data values and scale transforms cannot be reconstructed reliably from pixels
tooltips, brushing, zoom, selection, and animation require interaction evidence

facets.name: Scale, uncertainty, and accessible alternatives
facets.question: How should dense series, missing values, uncertainty, small screens, color vision, and non-visual access be handled?
inspect: series count, label collision, sampling, aggregation, and small-multiple implications
missing, estimated, forecast, confidence, error, and stale data cues
non-color encoding, text summaries, data tables, focus order, and responsive transformation
screenshotLimits: statistical validity and uncertainty cannot be inferred unless visibly explained
screen-reader and keyboard access require implementation evidence

axes.name: Interaction, state machines, feedback, and motion
axes.purpose: Define observable and proposed control states, business states, triggers, feedback, exits, modalities, and functional motion.

facets.name: Control states
facets.question: Which default, hover, focus, pressed, selected, disabled, read-only, and dragged states are shown or required?
inspect: state cues, anatomy stability, and programmatic-state implications
pointer, keyboard, touch, stylus, and assistive-input equivalence
focus visibility and target ownership
screenshotLimits: static screenshots do not observe most control states
visual state does not prove accessible or programmatic state

facets.name: Business and async states
facets.question: Which loading, empty, no-results, partial, stale, warning, error, success, conflict, and offline states are necessary?
inspect: state trigger, visible anatomy, message, action, exit, and context preservation
component-local versus page-level states
state priority, coexistence, and replacement behavior
screenshotLimits: unshown states are proposed or unknown, never observed
a static image cannot prove async transitions

facets.name: Feedback, confirmation, and recovery
facets.question: How does feedback match the scope, consequence, duration, interruption cost, and recovery path of an action?
inspect: inline feedback, status regions, toasts, banners, dialogs, progress, and optimistic updates
confirmation, cancellation, retry, undo, escalation, and manual recovery
message placement, persistence, duplication, and interruption budget
screenshotLimits: timing, repetition, announcement, and dismissal are not visible
visual success does not prove completed backend work

facets.name: Focus, overlays, and modalities
facets.question: How must focus, scroll, selection, and context behave across dialogs, drawers, popovers, menus, disclosure, and direct manipulation?
inspect: open, close, escape, outside-click, focus trap, focus return, and scroll lock requirements
trigger-result relationship and nested overlay risks
gesture alternatives, keyboard order, and programmatic state
screenshotLimits: focus, scroll, gesture, and keyboard behavior require executed evidence
an open overlay does not reveal its full lifecycle

facets.name: Motion and spatial continuity
facets.question: Where can motion explain cause, hierarchy, origin, destination, progress, or continuity without delaying action?
inspect: feedback, transition, enter, exit, reorder, progress, skeleton, and shared-element roles
duration hierarchy, interruption, layout stability, and reduced-motion alternatives
spatial origin, destination, focus, and context preservation
screenshotLimits: duration, easing, path, and interruption cannot be observed in a still image
motion absent from evidence remains proposed or unknown

axes.name: Responsive, platform, and device adaptation
axes.purpose: Preserve hierarchy and action across widths, orientations, safe areas, virtual keyboards, device classes, and platform conventions.

facets.name: Intrinsic reflow
facets.question: Which groups wrap, stack, scroll locally, resize, reorder, collapse, or remain fixed as space changes?
inspect: essential versus secondary content
intrinsic sizing, wrapping, min/max constraints, and local scroll
semantic order and preserved task priority
screenshotLimits: one viewport does not establish reflow behavior
cropped screenshots can imitate overflow

facets.name: Breakpoints and container behavior
facets.question: What evidence supports transitions between layout regimes and container widths?
inspect: viewport and container-query implications
navigation, grid, panel, table, chart, and action transformations
content-driven thresholds rather than device labels alone
screenshotLimits: exact breakpoints cannot be inferred from a single width
device category does not prove CSS or native layout thresholds

facets.name: Mobile and native shell
facets.question: Which system bars, safe areas, bottom regions, navigation models, gestures, and native conventions are visibly relevant?
inspect: status bar, navigation bar, home indicator, notch, cutout, and safe-area treatment
top app bar, bottom navigation, tab bar, sheets, back behavior, and edge gestures
web-like versus native platform cues
screenshotLimits: screen dimensions alone do not prove iOS, Android, or web runtime
system-owned behavior and haptics are not visible in a static capture

facets.name: Orientation and virtual keyboard
facets.question: How should layout, focus, overlays, and actions survive rotation, resize, and on-screen keyboard intrusion?
inspect: portrait, landscape, split-screen, resizable window, and fold implications
focused field visibility, keyboard avoidance, and anchored actions
viewport units, safe-area changes, and transient system UI
screenshotLimits: unshown orientations and keyboard states remain proposed
static dimensions do not establish resizable behavior

facets.name: Device and input conventions
facets.question: Which pointer, touch, keyboard, stylus, remote, and assistive-input assumptions affect layout and interaction?
inspect: target density, hover dependence, shortcuts, gestures, context menus, and precision
desktop window, tablet, phone, touch laptop, and large-screen implications
platform-consistent controls and escape routes
screenshotLimits: input hardware cannot be certified from screenshots
visual convention does not prove native behavior

axes.name: Accessibility, inclusion, and localization
axes.purpose: Turn visible accessibility implications into explicit semantics, modality, contrast, zoom, localization, and verification contracts.
focusAreas: Zoom, text size, targets, and cognition

facets.name: Semantics and names
facets.question: Which headings, landmarks, labels, descriptions, roles, names, values, and states are implied by the visible structure?
inspect: probable heading hierarchy and landmark grouping
control labels, descriptions, status announcements, and relationships
tables, charts, lists, forms, dialogs, and custom-control semantics
screenshotLimits: DOM roles, names, relationships, and live regions are not visible
visual order does not prove semantic order

facets.name: Keyboard and focus
facets.question: What focus order, visibility, containment, shortcuts, skip paths, and return behavior must be verified?
inspect: focus visibility and non-color distinction
logical order, trapping, restoration, roving focus, and composite widgets
keyboard equivalents for pointer and gesture actions
screenshotLimits: keyboard behavior cannot be certified from pixels
a shown focus ring may be simulated content

facets.name: Contrast and non-color meaning
facets.question: Which text, controls, focus, graphics, status, and data encodings require measured contrast and redundant meaning?
inspect: relative visual contrast and likely risk pairs
icons, text, shape, pattern, position, and labels supplementing color
high-contrast and forced-colors implications
screenshotLimits: screenshots cannot certify contrast ratios
display and compression alter apparent contrast

facets.name: Zoom, text size, targets, and cognition
facets.question: How must the interface survive enlarged text, zoom, reflow, low precision, reduced motion, and reduced cognitive load?
inspect: text resizing, clipping, overlap, target size, spacing, and reading width
clear labels, chunking, consistency, time pressure, and error prevention
motion, transparency, contrast, and sensory preference implications
screenshotLimits: actual target boxes and zoom behavior require implementation evidence
appearance cannot prove cognitive accessibility

facets.name: Localization, RTL, and cultural resilience
facets.question: How should language expansion, pluralization, formats, scripts, direction, and culturally dependent meaning change the UI?
inspect: long labels, alternate scripts, plural forms, and text expansion
dates, times, numbers, currencies, names, addresses, and sorting
logical direction, mirroring, icon directionality, and mixed-direction data
screenshotLimits: one locale does not prove localization support
cultural interpretation cannot be established from layout alone

axes.name: Content design, trust, privacy, and ethics
axes.purpose: Extract terminology, voice, actionability, provenance, permission, consequence, consent, and ethical-interaction requirements.

facets.name: Voice, tone, and terminology
facets.question: Which vocabulary, sentence patterns, tone, capitalization, and naming conventions create a coherent content voice?
inspect: labels, headings, CTA verbs, descriptions, metadata, empty states, and help language
formal, direct, reassuring, technical, editorial, or conversational tone cues
term consistency, abbreviations, jargon, and ambiguity
screenshotLimits: visible copy does not establish the full voice strategy
audience and brand intent cannot be inferred with certainty

facets.name: Actionable microcopy
facets.question: Do labels and messages explain what happened, why it matters, what changes, and what the user can do next?
inspect: specific action labels, inline guidance, errors, warnings, confirmations, and next steps
cause, scope, consequence, recovery, and ownership
ambiguity, blame, dead ends, and repeated messaging
screenshotLimits: copy cannot prove the underlying outcome
unshown errors and edge cases remain proposed or unknown

facets.name: Permissions, privacy, and consent
facets.question: How are access, collection, sharing, retention, visibility, and consent explained at the decision point?
inspect: permission labels, access badges, privacy explanations, and collection rationale
scope, actor, audience, duration, reversibility, and alternatives
consent, opt-in, opt-out, and secondary-use implications
screenshotLimits: UI copy does not prove real policy, authorization, or data handling
absence of explanation does not establish absence of a policy

facets.name: Provenance, freshness, and uncertainty
facets.question: Where does information come from, when was it updated, what is incomplete, and how confident should users be?
inspect: source, owner, timestamp, sync, stale, partial, estimated, generated, and verified cues
scope, limitations, confidence, and comparison context
refresh, inspect, correct, report, and trace actions
screenshotLimits: visible provenance labels do not prove data quality
freshness and generation processes require system evidence

facets.name: Consequences and ethical interaction
facets.question: Are consequences proportionate and legible without coercion, obstruction, hidden defaults, or deceptive emphasis?
inspect: destructive, financial, privacy, publishing, permission, and irreversible consequences
confirmation, review, undo, cooling-off, and informed-choice patterns
asymmetric choices, hidden costs, forced continuity, urgency, and manipulative defaults
screenshotLimits: appearance alone cannot establish organizational intent
real consequences and legal adequacy require authorized review

axes.name: Perceived performance and resilience
axes.purpose: Keep the interface stable, understandable, recoverable, and work-preserving during delay, scale, failure, and degradation.
focusAreas: Partial, stale, offline, and unavailable data

facets.name: Loading priority and progress
facets.question: Which content should appear first, reserve space, stream, defer, or show determinate progress?
inspect: critical versus supporting content and action readiness
skeleton, placeholder, spinner, progress, optimistic, and incremental patterns
flash avoidance and timing questions
screenshotLimits: pixels cannot prove loading order or latency
timing thresholds require runtime validation

facets.name: Visual stability
facets.question: Which regions, dimensions, anchors, and scroll positions must remain stable across content and state changes?
inspect: reserved geometry, aspect ratio, min-size, and state-consistent anatomy
late media, fonts, banners, errors, and dynamic content
focus, selection, scroll, and viewport stability
screenshotLimits: layout shift and flicker require a sequence or runtime measurement
stable appearance in one frame does not prove stable transitions

facets.name: Partial, stale, offline, and unavailable data
facets.question: How does the UI distinguish what is current, missing, delayed, cached, estimated, or unavailable?
inspect: partial-region versus whole-screen degradation
stale, sync, offline, unavailable, permission, and dependency states
continued reading, editing, retry, and freshness cues
screenshotLimits: network, cache, and backend behavior are not visible
an empty region does not identify its failure cause

facets.name: Recovery and work preservation
facets.question: How are retry, resume, draft, conflict, rollback, and escalation handled without discarding context or input?
inspect: local retry, page retry, reconnect, resume, restore, and support escalation
draft, queued, conflict, duplicate, timeout, and partial-success implications
input, selection, scroll, and navigation-context preservation
screenshotLimits: real persistence and rollback require system evidence
recovery behavior absent from screenshots remains proposed

facets.name: Scale, media, and rendering cost
facets.question: Which lists, charts, images, maps, effects, and content volumes risk perceptual or interaction cost?
inspect: long collections, dense charts, media grids, maps, blur, shadows, and animation
progressive media, placeholders, local scrolling, aggregation, and simplification
interaction readiness and degradation priorities
screenshotLimits: runtime cost, memory, virtualization, and network weight cannot be measured from screenshots
visual complexity does not prove poor performance

axes.name: Design system grammar and governance
axes.purpose: Convert evidence into semantic tokens, component contracts, scoped rules, coverage, provenance, integration guidance, and non-regression checks.

facets.name: Tokens and relationships
facets.question: Which semantic roles, scales, aliases, modes, and relationships are reusable without inventing exact values?
inspect: color, space, size, type, border, radius, elevation, opacity, layer, motion, icon, asset, and data roles
role relationships, scales, modes, aliases, and exceptional values
observed relationships versus proposed implementation bounds
screenshotLimits: exact token values require evidence or accepted calibration
target-project tokens are integration context, not source evidence

facets.name: Component and pattern contracts
facets.question: Which anatomy, variants, states, compositions, content limits, and anti-patterns can be generated consistently?
inspect: canonical component and UI-domain patterns
required parts, variants, states, relationships, and exceptions
generator guidance versus audit-only requirements
screenshotLimits: visual repetition does not prove shared source code
unseen variants remain proposed or unknown

facets.name: Provenance and coverage
facets.question: Is every axis facet and UI domain explicitly covered, partial, unknown, or not applicable with traceable evidence?
inspect: evidence, confidence, scope, exceptions, conflicts, and unknowns
facet coverage and UI-domain applicability
missing references and next evidence required
screenshotLimits: document presence does not prove semantic coverage
coverage cannot promote unsupported claims

facets.name: Framework-neutral design-to-code mapping
facets.question: How can the grammar guide implementation without binding extraction to a framework or target-project aesthetics?
inspect: semantic roles, component contracts, validation cases, and integration boundaries
generated versus guidance-only versus audit-only outputs
technical adapter opportunities and limitations
screenshotLimits: screenshots do not reveal framework or code architecture
repository conventions cannot become Design DNA observations

facets.name: Installation, audit, and non-regression
facets.question: Which rules require deterministic validation, perceptual review, usage evidence, ownership, migration, and rollback?
inspect: rule strength, verification method, owner, and failure impact
managed files, overrides, checksums, migration, and rollback
mechanical, perceptual, usage, and accessibility audit layers
screenshotLimits: agent guidance is not mechanical enforcement
code-level validation does not prove perceptual fidelity or usability

concepts.name: Spatial system and rhythm
concepts.description: Preserve region, grid, alignment, spacing, density, and depth relationships across generated layouts.
inspect: regions and nesting
tracks, gutters, margins, and spans
gap families, alignment, density, and depth
screenshotLimits: exact measurements are not established by scaled pixels
one viewport cannot prove responsive geometry

concepts.name: Typographic system and readability
concepts.description: Keep type roles, hierarchy, metrics, numerals, and overflow behavior coherent and legible.
inspect: semantic type roles
size, weight, line height, measure, and tracking relationships
numeric and multilingual treatment
screenshotLimits: font identity and exact metrics are not visually certain
one language does not prove script or locale resilience
stressTests: large signed values and alternate number formats

concepts.name: Semantic color and theme roles
concepts.description: Preserve meaning across canvas, surfaces, text, actions, statuses, focus, selection, and theme modes.
inspect: semantic color roles and pairings
status and interaction roles
light, dark, and high-contrast implications
screenshotLimits: source values and contrast ratios are not certified from screenshots
one theme does not establish another

concepts.name: Surface, shape, and depth hierarchy
concepts.description: Keep fills, borders, radii, elevation, overlays, and transparency proportional to containment and interaction.
inspect: surface tiers
border, radius, shadow, opacity, and overlay relationships
nested depth and selected states
screenshotLimits: exact shadow and opacity values are not visually provable
static depth does not prove dynamic elevation

concepts.name: Iconographic coherence
concepts.description: Prevent mixed, ambiguous, poorly aligned, unlabeled, or directionally incorrect icon language.
inspect: stroke, fill, caps, corners, optical size, and bounding box
alignment, color, semantic role, and labeling
directionality and state treatment
screenshotLimits: exact libraries and accessible names are invisible
RTL behavior cannot be certified

concepts.name: Asset and brand expression
concepts.description: Preserve coherent imagery, illustration, photography, logo, avatar, crop, and visual-personality choices.
inspect: asset roles, ratios, masks, crops, and density
brand motifs and emotional tone
fallback and loading implications
screenshotLimits: licenses, source quality, alt text, and full identity strategy are not visible
a loaded asset does not prove fallback behavior
stressTests: brand asset absent or low resolution

concepts.name: Component anatomy and composition
concepts.description: Prevent components from becoming inconsistent collections of slots, variants, states, and nested structures.
inspect: required, optional, repeatable, and conditional parts
variant, density, and composition relationships
exceptions and anti-patterns
screenshotLimits: visual repetition does not prove shared implementation
unshown variants are not observed

concepts.name: State and edge-case coverage
concepts.description: Prevent happy-path-only controls, components, collections, forms, and workflows.
inspect: displayed state, probable trigger, feedback, exit, and preserved context
control and business state anatomy
coexisting and nested states
screenshotLimits: unshown states and transitions are never observed
programmatic state is invisible without implementation evidence
stressTests: loading, empty, no-results, partial, stale, warning, error, success, conflict, disabled, and offline

concepts.name: Affordance and discoverability
concepts.description: Prevent actions that are visually ambiguous, hidden behind unsupported gestures, or inconsistent with their consequence.
inspect: interactive shape, contrast, label, icon, placement, and grouping
primary, secondary, contextual, and destructive cues
gesture and hover dependencies
screenshotLimits: appearance does not prove the full hit region or interaction
shortcuts and gestures are not visible

concepts.name: Navigation and orientation
concepts.description: Preserve current location, hierarchy, scope, return paths, and movement among visible contexts.
inspect: global and local navigation
active location and scope
breadcrumbs, tabs, steps, and return paths
screenshotLimits: one screen does not prove destinations or persistence
visual state does not prove routing or focus

concepts.name: Information hierarchy and reading order
concepts.description: Preserve the intended overview, evidence, decision, and action sequence without relying on accidental geometry.
inspect: visual order, grouping, salience, and probable semantic order
summary-to-detail and problem-to-action sequence
competing focal points
screenshotLimits: visual order does not prove DOM order or comprehension
prominence does not establish product priority

concepts.name: Progressive disclosure
concepts.description: Prevent both premature complexity and hidden essential information or actions.
inspect: primary and secondary information
menus, expanders, details, overlays, and staged workflows
initial density and paths to depth
screenshotLimits: closed content and transition behavior are invisible
placement does not establish usage frequency

concepts.name: Form and data-entry integrity
concepts.description: Keep labels, input models, formatting, dependencies, save behavior, and sensitive values understandable and recoverable.
inspect: labels, instructions, groups, input and selection models
format, precision, masking, and dependencies
save, cancel, draft, and sensitive-data implications
screenshotLimits: DOM associations, input modes, parsing, and persistence are invisible
one state does not establish workflow behavior

concepts.name: Validation, error prevention, and recovery
concepts.description: Prevent vague, destructive, poorly timed, or context-losing validation and failure behavior.
inspect: validation location, timing implication, specificity, and severity
correction focus and input preservation
retry, undo, conflict, and escalation
screenshotLimits: timing, backend rules, and persistence are not visible
absence of errors does not prove their design

concepts.name: Data comparison and decision context
concepts.description: Prevent metrics and statistics from appearing precise while omitting units, period, baseline, target, denominator, or freshness.
inspect: value, label, unit, timeframe, comparison, target, and freshness anatomy
precision, rounding, ranking, and segmentation
positive, negative, and neutral interpretation cues
screenshotLimits: formula and business meaning are not derivable from layout
color or arrows do not prove desirability

concepts.name: Visualization encoding integrity
concepts.description: Keep chart questions, marks, channels, axes, scales, legends, annotations, uncertainty, and alternatives coherent.
inspect: chart purpose, mark, channel, scale, baseline, legend, label, and annotation
series and comparison semantics
uncertainty, missing values, interaction, and accessible alternative
screenshotLimits: data values and transforms cannot be reconstructed reliably
tooltips and keyboard navigation are not visible

concepts.name: Data-scale resilience
concepts.description: Prevent tables, lists, cards, charts, filters, and navigation from working only with sample data.
inspect: collection density and anatomy
column, row, series, action, and label priority
pagination, aggregation, grouping, and overflow implications
screenshotLimits: real volume, virtualization, and backend limits are invisible
one data page does not prove extreme behavior
stressTests: no data, one item, thousands of rows, many series, long identifiers, extreme values

concepts.name: Content and layout resilience
concepts.description: Prevent text, values, media, actions, and states from breaking layout under realistic variation.
inspect: wrap, clamp, ellipsis, growth, and overflow zones
content-container dependencies
action and status preservation
screenshotLimits: short content does not prove overflow policy
fixed height does not prove zoom or localization resilience

concepts.name: Semantic responsiveness and reflow
concepts.description: Preserve meaning and task priority as regions wrap, stack, scroll, collapse, hide, or reorder.
inspect: intrinsic groups and containers
essential versus secondary elements
wrap, local scroll, reorganization, and order
screenshotLimits: one viewport reveals no breakpoint
unshown hide, collapse, and reorder behavior remains proposed or unknown

concepts.name: Platform and device conventions
concepts.description: Respect visible web, mobile, desktop, native-shell, safe-area, orientation, keyboard, and system-navigation implications.
inspect: system chrome, safe areas, top and bottom regions
back, menu, sheet, tab, window, and virtual-keyboard implications
device and input conventions
screenshotLimits: dimensions do not prove platform or runtime
haptics and system behavior are invisible

concepts.name: Input-modality equivalence
concepts.description: Ensure pointer, touch, keyboard, stylus, gesture, remote, and assistive-input users can reach equivalent outcomes.
inspect: visible target size and control grouping
hover, gesture, drag, and precision dependencies
probable focus and activation order
screenshotLimits: real hit boxes, focus order, gestures, and shortcuts are invisible
equivalence requires interaction evidence

concepts.name: Spatial continuity and context preservation
concepts.description: Keep location, focus, selection, scroll, and trigger-result relationships understandable across state and view changes.
inspect: navigation anchors and active context
trigger-result spatial relationship
focus, selection, scroll, and return implications
screenshotLimits: focus return and scroll restoration are invisible
continuity across screens requires a sequence or proposal

concepts.name: Localization and bidirectionality resilience
concepts.description: Prevent English-only geometry, formatting, direction, vocabulary, and sorting assumptions.
inspect: date, number, currency, unit, name, and address formats
label expansion, scripts, and plurals
logical direction, mirroring, and mixed-direction content
screenshotLimits: one language does not prove internationalization
RTL, plurals, and alternate formats remain unobserved

concepts.name: Accessibility semantics and annotations
concepts.description: Prevent visual accessibility claims without DOM, name, role, state, focus, contrast, zoom, and assistive-technology verification.
inspect: visual order and probable semantics
labels, relative contrast, focus cues, and non-color coding
tables, charts, forms, overlays, and custom control implications
screenshotLimits: conformance cannot be certified without implementation tests
roles, names, focus order, live regions, and screen-reader behavior remain unknown

concepts.name: Reversibility and forgiveness
concepts.description: Prevent high-cost mistakes and context loss through proportionate confirmation, cancellation, undo, drafts, and recovery.
inspect: consequential actions and visible safeguards
cancel, back, undo, draft, restore, and review patterns
precision of consequences
screenshotLimits: real undo and rollback are not proven
server-side effects remain unknown

concepts.name: Feedback proportionality and interruption budget
concepts.description: Prevent excessive, missing, duplicated, poorly placed, or inaccessible feedback.
inspect: message placement, intensity, persistence, and actionability
relationship among cause, scope, consequence, and recovery
inline, status, toast, banner, and dialog hierarchy
screenshotLimits: duration, repetition, announcement, and dismissal are invisible
appearance does not prove assistive announcement

concepts.name: Functional motion grammar
concepts.description: Use motion only to explain feedback, hierarchy, origin, destination, progress, or continuity while remaining interruptible and reducible.
inspect: spatial origin and destination
feedback versus transition hierarchy
interruption, layout stability, and reduced-motion alternative
screenshotLimits: duration, easing, path, and interruption are not observable in a still image
absent motion remains proposed or unknown

concepts.name: Visual stability
concepts.description: Prevent layout shift, flicker, scroll jumps, moving targets, and state-induced geometry loss.
inspect: reserved space and stable dimensions
loaded versus placeholder anatomy
focus, scroll, selection, and sticky or overlaid elements
screenshotLimits: layout shift and flicker require a sequence or runtime test
one stable frame does not prove stable transitions

concepts.name: Asset and media resilience
concepts.description: Prevent broken crops, missing fallbacks, loading shifts, inaccessible media, and inconsistent asset treatment.
inspect: ratio, crop, density, alignment, and role
reserved space, fallback, and placeholder implications
informative versus decorative role
screenshotLimits: source files, licenses, alt text, fallbacks, and loading are invisible
a loaded asset does not reveal failure behavior

concepts.name: Content voice and comprehension
concepts.description: Keep terminology, labels, CTA verbs, explanations, errors, and tone coherent, precise, inclusive, and actionable.
inspect: terminology and naming consistency
voice, tone, sentence shape, and action verbs
clarity, jargon, ambiguity, and next steps
screenshotLimits: visible copy does not establish comprehension or complete content strategy
audience intent remains inferred

concepts.name: Trust, permission, privacy, and transparency
concepts.description: Make access, source, freshness, uncertainty, collection, sharing, consequences, and control legible at the decision point.
inspect: provenance, freshness, scope, and limitations
permission, privacy, consent, sharing, and audience
consequence, reversibility, and ownership
screenshotLimits: real policy, data processing, and permissions are invisible
UI claims do not prove backend enforcement

concepts.name: Ethical interaction and informed choice
concepts.description: Prevent deceptive emphasis, forced continuity, hidden defaults, obstruction, manufactured urgency, and disproportionate friction.
inspect: choice symmetry and default visibility
cost, consequence, urgency, consent, opt-out, and cancellation
friction proportionality and user control
screenshotLimits: appearance alone does not establish intent or legal compliance
business rules and consequences require authorized evidence

concepts.name: Design-to-code and non-regression contract
concepts.description: Turn the extracted grammar into framework-neutral, installable, auditable, versioned, and override-safe guidance.
inspect: tokens, relations, component and domain contracts
rule strength, evidence, confidence, exceptions, coverage, and calibration
installation ownership, checksums, migration, rollback, and audit layers
screenshotLimits: screenshots do not reveal framework or code structure
guidance is not mechanical enforcement and code match is not perceptual proof

uiDomains.name: Application shell and navigation
uiDomains.description: Persistent and contextual structures that orient users and connect visible product areas.
inspect: shell regions and ownership
global and local navigation
current location and scope
collapse and small-screen transformation
screenshotLimits: one screen does not prove persistence or destinations

uiDomains.name: Marketing and editorial content
uiDomains.description: Heroes, narratives, feature sections, proof, calls to action, and long-form content composition.
inspect: headline and supporting copy hierarchy
section rhythm and narrative progression
proof and trust cues
primary and secondary calls to action
screenshotLimits: a screenshot does not establish campaign strategy, conversion, or audience

uiDomains.name: Actions and controls
uiDomains.description: Buttons, icon buttons, links, menus, toggles, segmented controls, and action groups.
inspect: anatomy, emphasis, size, and intent
primary, secondary, destructive, and contextual hierarchy
label and icon rules
control states and target implications
screenshotLimits: appearance does not prove activation, target size, or accessible name

uiDomains.name: Forms and data entry
uiDomains.description: Inputs, selections, validation, uploads, staged workflows, editing, and save behavior.
inspect: labels, instructions, groups, and controls
validation, error, and success behavior
formatting, sensitive values, and locale
save, cancel, draft, and recovery
screenshotLimits: static captures do not prove validation timing, associations, persistence, or keyboard behavior

uiDomains.name: Search, filter, and sort
uiDomains.description: Query, refinement, scope, active criteria, result counts, no-results, and reset patterns.
inspect: query and scope
filter representation and active criteria
result feedback, no-results, and reset
small-screen disclosure and preserved context
screenshotLimits: controls do not prove query behavior, debounce, sorting, or result semantics

uiDomains.name: Tables and lists
uiDomains.description: Dense and repeated collections with rows, columns, hierarchy, actions, selection, and navigation.
inspect: row and column anatomy
alignment, density, priority, and actions
sorting, grouping, selection, and pagination cues
overflow and small-screen transformation
screenshotLimits: one dataset does not prove scale, sorting, pagination, or virtualization

uiDomains.name: Cards and collections
uiDomains.description: Repeated bounded summaries, media items, tiles, and heterogeneous collections.
inspect: card anatomy and action ownership
grid, list, and featured variants
equal versus content-driven height
selection, loading, empty, and overflow behavior
screenshotLimits: repeated rectangles do not prove one component family

uiDomains.name: Statistics and KPIs
uiDomains.description: Primary values, supporting context, trends, comparisons, targets, timeframes, and freshness.
inspect: label, value, unit, context, trend, comparison, timeframe, target, and freshness
numeric precision and alignment
positive, negative, neutral, missing, and stale states
grid hierarchy and drill-down action
screenshotLimits: layout does not establish formula, business meaning, desirability, or freshness

uiDomains.name: Charts and data visualization
uiDomains.description: Visual encodings, axes, scales, legends, labels, annotations, interaction, uncertainty, and alternatives.
inspect: question and comparison
marks and encoding channels
axes, scales, baselines, legends, labels, and annotations
interaction, uncertainty, missing values, and accessible alternative
screenshotLimits: pixels do not prove exact data, scale transforms, tooltips, or keyboard access

uiDomains.name: Status and progress
uiDomains.description: Badges, indicators, progress, health, severity, state, and lifecycle communication.
inspect: label, icon, color, shape, and placement
determinate, indeterminate, lifecycle, and severity meaning
compact and verbose variants
non-color and announced equivalents
screenshotLimits: color and animation do not prove meaning, progress, or announcement

uiDomains.name: Overlays and disclosure
uiDomains.description: Dialogs, drawers, sheets, popovers, menus, tooltips, expanders, and inline detail.
inspect: trigger and placement
anatomy, hierarchy, and action ownership
open, close, cancel, escape, focus, and scroll requirements
nested and small-screen behavior
screenshotLimits: an open overlay does not reveal its lifecycle, focus, dismissal, or responsive behavior

uiDomains.name: Media and galleries
uiDomains.description: Images, video, audio, thumbnails, avatars, logos, galleries, previews, and crops.
inspect: role, ratio, crop, mask, and alignment
caption, action, selection, and preview anatomy
loading, missing, error, and fallback behavior
alternative text and responsive media implications
screenshotLimits: source quality, license, alt text, controls, and loading are not visible

uiDomains.name: Messaging and notifications
uiDomains.description: Conversation, activity, alerts, toasts, banners, inboxes, and unread state.
inspect: sender, time, status, body, attachment, and action anatomy
unread, pending, sent, failed, edited, deleted, and grouped states
priority, interruption, dismissal, and retention
provenance, privacy, and delivery implications
screenshotLimits: delivery, read state, timing, and announcement are not proven by appearance

uiDomains.name: Calendars and timelines
uiDomains.description: Date grids, schedules, events, ranges, time zones, dependencies, and chronological narratives.
inspect: time scale and granularity
event anatomy, overlap, range, status, and dependency
navigation, selection, creation, and editing cues
locale, time zone, keyboard, and small-screen behavior
screenshotLimits: real scheduling logic, drag behavior, conflicts, and time-zone rules are not visible

uiDomains.name: Maps and spatial UI
uiDomains.description: Maps, layers, markers, clusters, regions, routes, legends, and location detail.
inspect: base map and overlay hierarchy
marker, cluster, region, route, legend, and detail anatomy
zoom, pan, selection, search, and location cues
non-map alternative, loading, privacy, and scale implications
screenshotLimits: map data, permissions, gestures, and accessible alternatives are not proven

uiDomains.name: Commerce and transactions
uiDomains.description: Products, prices, carts, totals, checkout, payment, orders, and consequential confirmation.

step, review, payment, confirmation, and recovery
fees, recurrence, scope, privacy, and consequence disclosure
empty, unavailable, failed, partial, and duplicate states
screenshotLimits: screenshots do not prove inventory, payment, tax, refund, or legal behavior

uiDomains.name: Authentication and onboarding
uiDomains.description: Sign-in, verification, account recovery, setup, guidance, permissions, and first-run progression.
inspect: identity and recovery fields
step, progress, skip, back, and completion cues
error, lockout, verification, and recovery states
permission, privacy, and expectation setting
screenshotLimits: actual authentication, security, lockout, and recovery behavior are not visible

uiDomains.name: Settings and configuration
uiDomains.description: Grouped preferences, defaults, inheritance, scopes, save models, destructive controls, and advanced options.
inspect: scope, grouping, dependency, default, inheritance, and reset
immediate, staged, autosave, and draft behavior
advanced, destructive, permission, and privacy settings
changed, saving, saved, failed, and conflict states
screenshotLimits: persistence, inheritance, permissions, and side effects are not visible

uiDomains.name: Mobile native shell
uiDomains.description: Status and navigation bars, safe areas, top and bottom app regions, sheets, gestures, and mobile system conventions.
inspect: system-owned and app-owned regions
safe-area and edge treatment
top app bar, tabs, bottom navigation, sheet, and back patterns
orientation, virtual keyboard, gesture, and target implications
screenshotLimits: dimensions and chrome do not prove platform runtime, haptics, or back behavior

uiDomains.name: Files and content management
uiDomains.description: Upload, preview, version, folder, metadata, selection, transfer, processing, and content lifecycle.
inspect: file and folder anatomy, type, size, owner, version, and status
